title: Multi-Surrogate-Objective Optimization for Neural Topic Models
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
task: Balancing several loss terms when training neural topic models
problem: NTM losses (reconstruction, KL, regularisers) differ by orders of magnitude; fixed weights need costly tuning and naive multi-objective optimisation (MOO) can hurt.
architecture: MSOO: each loss is replaced by a surrogate L_i + lambda_i * (sum of all losses), fed to a gradient-based MOO algorithm (FairGrad or MGDA); static (constant lambda) and adaptive (lambda from relative descent rates) variants; applied to ECRTM and NeuroMax.
key_results: ECRTM on AGNews: Purity 0.802 baseline, 0.772 with plain FairGrad MOO, 0.834 with MSOO-Adaptive.
NeuroMax on 20NG: Purity 0.623 baseline vs 0.645 with MSOO-Static.
lambda between 0.4 and 0.8 works best; very small lambda collapses NMI (0.021 at lambda = 0.001).
strengths: Shows that direct MOO can underperform the baseline and gives a simple fix.
Model-agnostic, tested on two strong NTMs and three datasets.

limitations.text: Higher computational cost and longer training; surrogate is a simple linear combination.
Gains are small on some metrics and TD sometimes drops (e.g. ECRTM 20NG TD15 0.964 to 0.901 with MSOO-S).
